issues.description: File filter '*.exe' hides conda binaries on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: In confpage.py the create_browsefile call uses filters='*.exe', which only matches Windows executables. On macOS and Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba have no extension, so the file picker will hide them by default and force users to type the path manually. Use a cross-platform filter (e.g., '*' or platform-specific).

issues.description: validate_conda substring check accepts arbitrary binaries
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"])` will accept any executable whose --version output happens to contain 'mamba' or 'conda' anywhere (including arbitrary path/banner text). It also fails to anchor on the program name. Consider matching at the start of the output or parsing more strictly.

issues.description: validate_conda may hang UI on unresponsive executable
issues.detail: validate_conda runs the chosen binary via run_program(...).communicate() with no timeout. If the user picks a misbehaving binary (or one that prompts), the preferences UI will block indefinitely. Add a timeout and kill the process on expiry.

validate_conda rejects paths where os.access(path, os.X_OK) is False. On Windows, os.X_OK behavior for arbitrary files is unreliable and may return False for valid .exe files in some contexts, especially network paths. Since the subprocess run will already fail for non-executable files, this check is redundant and may cause false negatives.

issues.description: Custom conda path used without validating it works at runtime
issues.detail: kernelspec.py reads conf 'conda_path' and uses it directly as conda_exe without re-validating. If the user previously set a valid path that has since been moved/deleted, or the config was edited externally, conda_version() and downstream calls will fail with confusing errors rather than the helpful 'set the path' message.

issues.description: Unconditional setFocus after select_file may affect other browsefile users
issues.detail: create_browsefile's select_file now calls edit.setFocus() whenever a filename is chosen. This is a behavior change for every existing user of create_browsefile across Spyder, not just the new conda field. Worth verifying no other preference pages rely on focus remaining elsewhere after browsing.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful escape hatch for users with non-standard conda installs, and the structure (config key, conf page widget, validator, kernelspec fallback) is sensible. Main concerns: the file dialog filter '*.exe' makes the picker unusable on macOS/Linux, validate_conda has weak version-string matching plus no subprocess timeout, and the kernelspec path uses the configured conda blindly without revalidation. There is also an incidental behavior change in create_browsefile (unconditional setFocus) that affects all callers.
